title: Qoder: keep working on the last catalog when a background refresh fails
hypothesis: catalog_refresh_failed burns the bounded request-retry budget and reaches the user, although the previous catalog still routes.
measurement: Offline tests only (catalog-refresh.test.mjs, 22; two new cases fail with the change reverted). No model calls. Metric for the next 28-day harvest: qoder user-visible catalog_refresh_failed plus catalog_refresh_required falls from 11 of 75 to 0, with no rise in malformed-request codes.
result: Absorbs catalog_refresh_failed only when a previous catalog is loaded: no retry, reuse flagged, local expiry untouched; with no previous catalog it still surfaces, and account switches or aborts are not absorbed. Effective version: product build 0.1.27, the release that first carries this provider.mjs. The Qoder extension ships inside the product bundle, not in the Pi fork, so the fork version (1.4.0-rotom.3) is not what gates this fix; a session still running an older product build keeps the old behaviour until it is restarted on a release that contains it. Acceptance window opened 2026-11-10T13:30:07Z (local 2026-11-10 05:30): the daily install switched to product 0.1.27-main.2b4ea53b, built from commit 2b4ea53b. That release carries this provider.mjs, so the acceptance window for catalog_refresh_failed absorption opens at that moment; sessions still on the previous product build keep the old behaviour. Acceptance metric declared for the weekly report: provider_error where category=qoder:catalog_refresh_failed per 100 user turns, baseline 0.00 over the 4,146 user turns that preceded the switch; the first status is read once 300 post-switch turns exist. Baseline source: 11 user-visible `qoder:catalog_refresh_failed` incidents in the 4,178 user turns recorded before the switch. Round 7 declared 0.00 because the metric filtered the report bucket (`category`), which a trace span overwrites with the transport bucket; the provider's own code is now harvested as `code`, so the numerator is countable. This is a definition fix, not a window or rate change.  Acceptance now counts only sessions whose release traces to 854dd51b or a descendant; 0.1.27-main.2b4ea53b windows do not count because its Qoder provider could not load, so no Qoder turn in them reached the transport.

title: Retry policy: honour Retry-After on 429 and stop retrying quota errors
hypothesis: Retrying a 429 on the built-in backoff arrives before the server window; retrying a 402/balance error cannot succeed and hides the one action a user can take.
measurement: Offline tests only (packages/ai retry.test.ts and retry-limits.test.ts, 76 cases; 5 fail with the change reverted). No model calls. Metric for the next 28-day harvest: user-visible http and 429 failures fall from 62 + 6 of 847 provider incidents, and no quota error costs more than one attempt.
result: 429 delays use retryAfterMs or Retry-After, capped at the existing maximum, with exponential backoff as fallback; quota/402/balance errors are non-retryable and the final message adds one actionable hint. Bounded and connect retry unchanged. Correction from round 4: this shipped only as source at first push. The Pi fork was not rebuilt then, so the runtime the product loads still had the old retry path; 8204224 alone could not change behaviour. commit 6ae816d7 rebuilt the fork as 1.4.0-rotom.3 (vendored archives, fork-build.json, runtime/pi lock, product-config version and integrity all follow it), and an isolated install from that lockfile greps the new code in the installed pi-ai dist. The acceptance window therefore starts the day the daily install is switched to 1.4.0-rotom.3, not the day of 8204224. Acceptance window opened 2026-11-10T13:30:07Z (local 2026-11-10 05:30): the daily install switched to product 0.1.27-main.2b4ea53b, built from commit 2b4ea53b. That release carries Pi fork 1.4.0-rotom.3, so the acceptance window for the Retry-After and quota behaviour opens at that moment rather than at 8204224. Acceptance metric declared for the weekly report: provider_error where category=429 per 100 user turns, baseline 0.14 over the 4,146 user turns that preceded the switch; the first status is read once 300 post-switch turns exist.

title: One weekly command that cannot leak the field comparison before its window closes
hypothesis: The weekly review was four manual steps over the harvest artifact, and the field comparison had no way to show progress without also showing the result it is supposed to keep blinded, so the natural habit was to look early and decide late.
measurement: No model calls. `loop weekly` harvests the last 28 days in-process and writes ~/.rotom/loop/weekly-<date>/ (0700 directory, 0600 files, not in Git). The blinded section is a separate type with no outcome field, so an in-window render cannot print a v2 rate: the test asserts the rendered section contains the arm names and neither 'v2' nor 'per 100'. Every shipped-but-unmeasured ledger record now may declare an `acceptance` (metric name, incident kind, optional detail filter, baseline per 100 turns, minimum turns, direction) that the parser validates and the report reads using only sessions after `startedAt`. Records without one report `no-metric` instead of a guessed number. Provider failures are split at the switch instant and attributed to the segment their session started in. 9 new tests; the whole evals suite and typecheck pass.
result: First run on 2026-11-10: 713 sessions, 1,679 incidents, overall 6.0 v2 per 100 turns (5.2-6.7), 5.3 without the largest session; per model gpt-6.1-sol 10.1 with 7.5 without its largest session, gpt-6-astra 4.7, dfmodel 6.4; per product version 0.1.27 at 4.1 and 0.1.27-main.0d90623 at 16.6 with 9.6 without the largest session. The field comparison reports 0 sessions per arm because the window opens 2026-11-11. Of 15 shipped-unmeasured records, 5 declare a metric and are not-yet-due (1 turn since the switch), 10 report no-metric. Provider failures before the switch: openai-codex 19.8 per 100 turns, qoder 5.3. The five acceptance baselines were computed from the pre-switch half of the same harvest (4,146 user turns), not estimated.

title: A replay that cannot publish, cannot see credentials and starts from the recorded branch
hypothesis: Re-running a recorded failure by hand is what the loop never did, because a naive replay would run a real model with real tools inside a live project and could publish, read a token from the environment, or start from the wrong code.
measurement: No model calls for the tooling itself; one real replay to prove the pipeline. `loop replay --incident <sessionId:entryId>` cuts the session at the failing user message (header kept, that message is the only new turn), pins the last commit at or before the session start (`rev-list -1 --before`), and refuses when the cwd is not a git repository or that instant has no commit. Isolation: a `clone --shared` copy instead of a registered worktree, all remotes removed, tools limited to read/edit/bash, HOME and PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR inside the replay directory, the environment stripped of *_TOKEN/*_KEY/*_SECRET/NPM_*/GH_*/GITHUB_*/AWS_*/SSH_AUTH_SOCK, and a BASH_ENV shim that exits 97 and prints a refusal for git push, npm publish, gh, ssh, scp, rsync and curl/wget writes. 13 tests cover branch cutting and its refusal paths, the timepoint selection, the environment scrub, the shim rules and the shim running for real in bash. Artifacts only under ~/.rotom/loop/replay-<stamp>/, never in Git.
result: One real replay, incident 01a1c36e:e2191f8b (user_correction in the trade-telemetry checkout, qoder/dfmodel): 49 earlier user turns replayed from commit f5b24c84, frozen product 0.1.27-main.50ccdc87, exit 0, 2,447 tool calls, no refusal, transcripts and the resulting session under the private replay directory, 4m35s. The 3-events-times-5-repeats admission run was NOT executed this round: at about five minutes per replay that is roughly 75 minutes of real sessions, and running it beside the round's own verification would contend for the same machine and provider. Admission stays unmeasured; the next step is the same command with --repeats 5 per event and a per-event deterministic check. Replay cases stay local-private: the ledger records only the mechanism, never the transcript, the case file or the session id.
